title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
summary: A chapter-by-chapter title. Pass each chapter as you read it, then sit the whole-book test at the end.

questions.q: What is Alice's complaint about the book her sister is reading?
options: It has no pictures or conversations
questions.why: Her boredom with a picture-less book is what makes a talking rabbit worth following.

questions.q: What makes the White Rabbit worth chasing, rather than just odd?
options: It takes a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket
questions.why: Alice only starts after it once it produces a pocket watch — a rabbit in a waistcoat with somewhere to be.

questions.q: What does Alice notice on the shelves as she falls?
options: Cupboards, bookshelves, maps and a jar labelled orange marmalade
questions.why: The fall is furnished like a house, which is the first sign the rules have changed.

questions.q: Why can Alice not use the little golden key at first?
options: She is far too large for the door it opens
She drops it down a crack
questions.why: The key fits the tiny door to the garden, which sets up the whole drink-me and eat-me problem.

questions.q: What happens when Alice drinks from the bottle marked DRINK ME?
options: She shuts up like a telescope and shrinks
questions.why: Shrinking gets her to the right size for the door, but leaves the key on a table she can no longer reach.

questions.q: How does Alice greet her sudden growth at the start of the chapter?
questions.why: Her own grammar falls apart along with her size, which she notices and half apologises for.

questions.q: What odd plan does Alice make once her feet are a long way off?
options: To write them a letter of complaint
To send them presents at Christmas
questions.why: She imagines posting boots to her own feet, addressed to the hearth-rug — silly in a way she takes entirely seriously.

questions.q: What does the White Rabbit drop when Alice startles him?
options: A pair of white kid gloves and a fan
questions.why: The fan is the important one: fanning herself is what shrinks her again.

questions.q: What is the pool Alice ends up swimming in?
options: A pool of her own tears
questions.why: She wept while she was nine feet tall, so the pool is the exact size of her earlier misery.

questions.q: How does Alice offend the Mouse?
options: By talking about her cat Dinah
questions.why: She cannot stop mentioning what a good mouser Dinah is — a habit that gets her into trouble again later.

chapters.title: 3. A Caucus-Race and a Long Tale

questions.q: Who proposes the Caucus-race, and why?
options: The Mouse, to warm everyone up
The Dodo, as the best way to get dry
questions.why: The Dodo's answer to being soaked is a race, explained in the most official language possible.

questions.q: What are the rules of the Caucus-race?
options: There is no proper start or finish, and everyone runs as they please
Last one to the rock wins
questions.why: Nobody calls time; they simply stop, and the joke is that a race with no rules still needs a prize-giving.

options: Everybody has won, and all must have prizes
It is abandoned in the rain
questions.why: The Dodo's verdict is the line the whole scene is built to reach.

questions.q: Where do the prizes come from?
options: Alice's pocket, which holds a box of comfits
questions.why: Alice supplies the prizes and is then handed her own thimble back as hers, presented very solemnly.

questions.q: Why do the birds leave at the end of the chapter?
options: They are late for the Queen
questions.why: She repeats exactly the mistake she made with the Mouse, and clears the bank of company.

verdicts.high: Curiouser and curiouser — and very well read.
verdicts.pass: Well done. On to the next chapter.
verdicts.fail: Below the passing mark. Read it again and come back.

questions.q: What sets the whole adventure off?
options: Alice falls asleep over a lesson book
Alice follows a White Rabbit with a pocket watch down a hole
Alice is pushed by her sister
questions.why: The rabbit, the waistcoat and the watch together are the invitation she cannot refuse.

questions.q: What repeated mistake keeps costing Alice company in the early chapters?
options: Mentioning her cat Dinah to animals
questions.why: First the Mouse, then the birds — she means no harm and empties the room twice.

questions.q: What is Alice's own prize in the Caucus-race?
options: Her own thimble, handed back to her
questions.why: She provides every prize and receives her own property with full ceremony.

questions.q: How does Wonderland treat rules and ceremony in these chapters?
options: It keeps the ceremony and drops the sense
It punishes anyone who breaks them
questions.why: A race with no start, a prize-giving with no prizes, a verdict with no contest — the forms survive, the logic does not.
